regions.summary: Lower Wu River borderland: Pengshui (Chongqing, 42%), Wuchuan and Daozhen (Zunyi, 30% and 23%).

candidates.name: Pengshui
candidates.meaning: "Peng River": the county took its name in 593 from the river now called the Yu River, then known as the Peng.
candidates.fit: Holds 80% of Pengshui county and 42% of the region's people, its biggest single part.
candidates.source_url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/彭水苗族土家族自治县
candidates.source_note: 隋开皇十三年（593年）置彭水县…县以江名

candidates.name: Wuchuan
candidates.meaning: County name since 599; the Yuan court respelled it 婺川 after a falling star was read as the Wu star, and it went back to 务川 in 1959.
candidates.fit: Holds 98% of the county and 30% of the region; the county seat (Duru) was also the seat of Song Sizhou.
candidates.source_url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/务川仡佬族苗族自治县
candidates.source_note: 务川于隋开皇十九年（599年）置县至今

candidates.name: Daozhen
candidates.meaning: Named for Yin Zhen, courtesy name Daozhen, a Han-dynasty scholar who taught the local people.
candidates.fit: Holds 98% of the county and 23% of the region; the Gelao homeland.
candidates.source_url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/道真仡佬族苗族自治县
candidates.source_note: 相传汉儒尹珍（字道真）先生在此兴教办学教化先民，因而得名

regions.notes: Region crosses into Chongqing; Pengshui is a Chongqing county.

regions.summary: Upper Furong River: Zheng'an and Suiyang (36% and 34%) with parts of Tongzi and Fenggang.

candidates.name: Furongjiang
candidates.meaning: Furong River (also called Pangu River), the largest tributary of the Wu River.
candidates.fit: Rises in Suiyang and runs through Zheng'an, so it crosses the two main counties of the region; 87% of its length is in Guizhou.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 72 hits with 贵州, top ones about this river.
candidates.source_note: 发源于贵州省绥阳县境内的大娄山，由西南向东北…汇入乌江

candidates.name: Zheng'an
candidates.meaning: "Upright and secure": Qing name from 1724, changed from Zhen'an 真安 to avoid a character in the Yongzheng emperor's name.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of the county, 36% of the region; the Tang prefecture Zhenzhou was seated at Anchang here.
candidates.source_note: 清朝雍正二年（1724年），避雍正帝讳改为正安州

candidates.name: Suiyang
candidates.meaning: Sui-dynasty county name; 绥 means to soothe or pacify, though here it is just the old county name, not a frontier phrase.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of the county, 34% of the region, and the upper Furong River.
candidates.source_note: 隋朝时，置绥阳县，后废…于万历二十九年（1601年）以旧绥阳县地，置绥阳县

regions.notes: Zhenzhou (珍州, Tang prefecture, 31 hits with 贵州) was left out: zh-wiki puts its seat at Tongzi's Yelang town while CHGIS puts it at Zheng'an.

regions.summary: Loushan pass country: Xishui (43%) and Tongzi (40%) plus a slice of Qijiang in Chongqing.

candidates.name: Tongzi
candidates.meaning: "Paulownia and catalpa": two tree names; county created in 1601 after the defeat of the Bozhou Yang chieftaincy.
candidates.fit: Holds 69% of Tongzi county and 40% of the region, including the county seat at Loushanguan.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; known for the 200,000-year-old Tongzi Man site and the Tongzi military clique.
candidates.source_note: 明万历二十九年（1601年），置桐梓县

candidates.name: Loushan
candidates.meaning: The Dalou (Loushan) range, the divide between the Wu River and the Chishui, with the Loushan pass on its crest.
candidates.fit: The pass sits at Loushanguan, the region's largest town (17%), on the Tongzi and Huichuan border.
candidates.recognisability: Loushan pass has its own zh-wiki article, 175 hits with 贵州, top ones about the pass.
candidates.source_note: 娄山关又名娄关，是大娄山脉的主峰，位于中国贵州省北部…北距桐梓县城13公里

candidates.name: Xishui
candidates.meaning: "Xi River": the county is named after the Xi River, a tributary of the Chishui.
candidates.fit: Holds 71% of Xishui county and 43% of the region's people, the largest part.
candidates.source_note: 主要河流还有…赤水河、习水河、桐梓河等

regions.notes: Qijiang (Chongqing) is already named on the map; nothing here repeats it.

regions.summary: Wu River gorge country: Dejiang (37%), Yanhe (35%), Yinjiang (26%).

candidates.name: Dejiang
candidates.meaning: "De River": the old name Shui Dejiang for the lower Wu River, from which the county takes its name.
candidates.fit: Holds 98% of the county and 37% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 德江，一称水德江，即乌江之下流…以境内德江河为名

candidates.name: Yanhe
candidates.meaning: "Along the river": the county lies on the Wu River; it grew from the Yanhe Youxi chieftaincy of 1376.
candidates.fit: Holds 77% of Yanhe Tujia county and 35% of the region; the Wu River gorge scenic area and Tujia mountain songs are here.
candidates.source_note: 位于贵州省东北部…沿河乌江山峡风景名胜区

regions.notes: Dejiang and Yanhe are about equal. Sizhou (Tang prefecture seated at Yanhe) was left out because the Ming Sizhou is a different, better-known place.

regions.summary: Chishui valley and Renhuai liquor country: Renhuai (55%), plus parts of Zunyi county, Huichuan and Honghuagang.

candidates.name: Renhuai
candidates.meaning: "Cherishing benevolence": Song-era fort name for tribal lands that submitted in 1109, so a mild frontier name; the place is now known as the liquor capital.
candidates.fit: Holds 97% of Renhuai city and 55% of the region, on the Chishui River.
candidates.source_note: 仁怀被誉为中国酒都…宋王朝在这些地区建立滋州、纯州、祥州等州。滋州领仁怀县

candidates.name: Maotai
candidates.meaning: "Thatch platform": the Gelao people covered their sacrificial platform with thatch, hence Maotai; it is the home of Moutai liquor.
candidates.fit: Maotai town holds only 4% of the region, but the name is what the whole Chishui stretch is known for.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 64 hits with 贵州, top ones about the town and the liquor.
candidates.source_note: 古獠人在祭祀台上栽满茅草，称祭祀台为茅草祭台，简称茅台，此地因而得名

regions.notes: The small label 'zunyi' on the picture sits partly over this region, but it belongs to the tiny region 8 beside it (city centre). Hailongtun (Bozhou Yang fortress, UNESCO) is in Gaoping town here but is a very small share. A Chishui River name would clash if Chishui city is named in a neighbouring batch.

regions.summary: Tongren city and Jiangkou, Songtao, Wanshan: the eastern edge near Fanjingshan.

candidates.name: Tongren
candidates.meaning: Originally "bronze man" 铜人: fishermen were said to have found three bronze statues in the river; the Ming changed the second character to 仁 "benevolence".
candidates.fit: Holds the city centre (Bijiang, 46% of the region) and the seat of the prefecture.
candidates.source_note: 铜仁原名铜人…及置长官司，始易人为仁

candidates.name: Fanjingshan
candidates.meaning: "Pure Buddhist land" mountain, the main peak of the Wuling range (2,572 m), a World Heritage site since 2018.
candidates.fit: The range lies at the Jiangkou, Yinjiang and Songtao meeting point; Jiangkou (20%) and part of Songtao are in this region, Yinjiang mostly in region 4.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 576 hits with 贵州, top ones about the mountain.
candidates.source_note: 梵净山位于中国贵州铜仁市的印江县、江口县、松桃县交界处，为武陵山脉主峰

regions.notes: Fenghuang (Hunan) neighbour is already named; no clash.

regions.summary: Middle Wu River: Sinan (47%), Shiqian (30%), Fenggang (21%).

candidates.name: Sinan
candidates.meaning: Ming prefecture and pacification commission of Sinan, seated at Sitang town on the Wu River; the old county was Anhua.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of Sinan county and 47% of the region; the Ming Sinan prefecture seat is at Sitang, the largest town.
candidates.source_note: 位于贵州东北部，乌江斜贯…明置安化县，为思南府治，1913年改设思南县

candidates.name: Wujiang
candidates.meaning: "Black River", the Wu River, the largest river of Guizhou, flowing north to the Yangtze at Fuling.
candidates.fit: The river crosses the middle of the region through Sinan; it also runs through region 1 and region 4.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; very well known.
candidates.source_note: 乌江干流横穿贵州中部和东北部，于重庆市涪陵区汇入长江

candidates.name: Shiqian
candidates.meaning: "Stone path": a Ming prefecture seat and now the county famous for its hot springs.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of Shiqian county and 30% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 石阡县是贵州矿泉最多的县

regions.notes: Wujiang (乌江) is also a town in Anhui (Xiang Yu's last stand); only a clash if that is named on the map.

regions.summary: Tiny patch holding the Zunyi city centre (Honghuagang and Huichuan); the 'zun / yi' label sits beside it.
regions.notes: Treated as settled because the label reads zunyi right next to this small region and the city centre is here. If the label was meant for region 5 instead, this region and region 9 need names.

regions.summary: Zunyi county country around the city: Zunyi county (now Bozhou district, 73%) with parts of Honghuagang and Huichuan.

candidates.name: Bozhou
candidates.meaning: Tang prefecture name (639) and seat of the Yang chieftaincy that ruled here for some 700 years; the old Zunyi county was renamed Bozhou district in 2016.
candidates.fit: Holds 70% of the old Zunyi county and 73% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; own zh-wiki article; the Bozhou campaign of 1600 is well known.
candidates.source_note: 2016年，中国国务院批准原遵义县改为播州区

candidates.name: Zunyi
candidates.meaning: "Follow the right": from the Book of Documents line 遵王之义; Tang county name since 642.
candidates.fit: The old Zunyi county is 73% of the region, but the name is already on the map for the city centre.
candidates.source_note: 遵义之名相传出自《尚书》：无偏无陂，遵王之义

regions.notes: Bozhou shares its spelling with Bozhou (亳州) in Anhui; different characters, so no clash.

candidates.name: Bijie
candidates.meaning: A Yi tribal name, said to be from Yi "Biji"; folk etymologies link it to the Bi River or to a New Year's Eve fortress wall.
candidates.fit: Holds the old Bijie county seat (Ming Bijie garrison) and 80% of Qixingguan, the prefecture's city; the central region takes the city name.
candidates.source_note: 毕节是彝语比跻的谐音，乃彝族部族名

candidates.name: Qixingguan
candidates.meaning: "Seven star pass": district name for a pass on the Bijie road; Qixing is the Big Dipper.
candidates.fit: The district is 99% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 七星关区是中华人民共和国贵州省毕节市下辖的一个市辖区

regions.summary: Mei and Weng rivers tea country: Weng'an (37%, Qiannan), Meitan (35%), Yuqing (24%).

candidates.name: Meitan
candidates.meaning: "Mei River pool": the county is on the Mei River; Guizhou's top tea county (Meitan Cuiya, Zunyi Hong).
candidates.fit: Holds 95% of Meitan county and 35% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 湄潭是…茶城、酒乡、烟县、粮仓…贵州第一茶县

candidates.name: Weng'an
candidates.meaning: From the Weng River (瓮水) and the Weng River pacification commission of the Ming; county since 1601.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of Weng'an county and 37% of the region, the largest part.
candidates.source_note: 瓮安县…位于贵州省中部

regions.notes: Yuqing (余庆, 24%) was left out as the smallest of the three.

regions.summary: Dafang county (71%) and eastern Jinsha (28%): the old Yi heartland of Mu'ege.

candidates.name: Dafang
candidates.meaning: "Great and square": the 1958 replacement for Dading 大定 "great stability", an old pacification name.
candidates.fit: Holds 84% of Dafang county and 71% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 清朝康熙五年设大定府；民国二年废府设大定县；1958年更名为大方县

candidates.name: Mu'ege
candidates.meaning: Yi name for the Shuixi polity and its capital, Mu'ege ancient city, which stands in Dafang town.
candidates.fit: The capital's site is in this region; the polity covered much of Bijie.
candidates.recognisability: 57 hits with 贵州, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 水西，彝语音译慕俄格或慕俄勾…明清以来汉人习惯称之为水西

candidates.name: Jinsha
candidates.meaning: "Gold sand"; county on the Chishui, more familiar as the name of the upper Yangtze.
candidates.fit: Only 47% of Jinsha county is here, so it fits poorly.
candidates.source_note: 金沙县…北隔赤水河邻接四川省

regions.notes: Mu'ege and Shuixi (region 14) are the same Yi polity under two names; use only one if Anita prefers.

regions.summary: Hezhang county (68%) and western Qixingguan, up to the Wumeng summit Jiucaiping.

candidates.name: Hezhang
candidates.meaning: County created in 1942 from northeast Weining; no meaning recorded in the sources I read.
candidates.fit: Holds 95% of Hezhang county and 68% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 赫章县…贵州最高峰韭菜坪位于此县，海拔2900.6米

candidates.name: Wumeng
candidates.meaning: The Wumeng mountains, the Yangtze and Pearl River divide; its main peak Jiucaiping (2,900 m) lies on the Hezhang border.
candidates.fit: The peak is in Hezhang, so this is the range's heart in Guizhou; the range reaches much further into Yunnan.
candidates.source_note: 乌蒙山主峰韭菜坪位于贵州六盘水和毕节赫章县交界地区，海拔2900米，为贵州最高峰

regions.notes: Kele (可乐, Yelang-era site in Hezhang) was dropped: 'Kele' reads as the word for cola.

regions.summary: Qianxi city and the Ya River: Qianxi (69%) and western Jinsha (29%).

candidates.name: Shuixi
candidates.meaning: "West of the water": the Yi Anshi chieftaincy (Shuixi xuanweisi, 1373-1664), west of the Ya River; Chinese name for Mu'ege.
candidates.fit: The Shuixi seat is at Qianxi, 69% of the region; the chieftaincy ruled most of Bijie.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 615 hits with 贵州, top ones about this chieftaincy and its wars.
candidates.source_note: 水西宣慰司 (1373-1664) 今贵州省黔西县治 (CHGIS)

candidates.name: Qianxi
candidates.meaning: "West Guizhou": Qing prefecture of 1666, made from Anshi land; now a county-level city.
candidates.fit: Holds 99% of Qianxi and 69% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 清康熙五年以安氏的则窝、以著、雄所则溪地置黔西府，改土设流

regions.notes: Qianxi is a Qing 'convert chieftaincy to regular rule' name; Shuixi is the older local name. Shuixi and Mu'ege (region 12) are the same polity.

regions.summary: Weining plateau: Weining county (99%), with Caohai lake.

candidates.name: Caohai
candidates.meaning: "Grass sea": Guizhou's largest natural lake (about 20 km2), choked with water plants; winter home of the black-necked crane.
candidates.fit: The lake is at the county seat; Caohai town holds 20% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 361 hits with 贵州, top ones about this lake.
candidates.source_note: 草海又名松坡湖、南海子、八仙湖，位于威宁彝族回族苗族自治县县城西南隅，因湖中水草繁茂，故名

candidates.name: Wusa
candidates.meaning: Yi name of the Wusa tribe and its prefecture, seated at today's Weining from 1278 to 1728.
candidates.fit: The seat was at Weining, 99% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: 67 hits with 贵州, top ones about Wusa prefectures; no article for the bare name.
candidates.source_note: 乌撒府…治所在乌撒（今贵州省威宁彝族回族苗族自治县）

candidates.name: Weining
candidates.meaning: "Might and peace": the Qing name from 1664, a pacify-the-frontier name in a county with Yi, Hui and Miao majorities.
candidates.fit: Holds 79% of the county and 99% of the region.
candidates.source_url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/威宁彝族回族苗族自治县
candidates.source_note: 威宁府 (1664-1728) 威宁州 (1729-1911) 今贵州省威宁县治 (CHGIS)

regions.notes: Weining is listed only because it is what the place is known as; Caohai or Wusa ranks above it.

regions.summary: Nayong county (67%), with parts of Shuicheng and Dafang.

candidates.name: Nayong
candidates.meaning: County created in 1941; no meaning recorded in the sources I read. Home of a third of the Chuanqing people.
candidates.fit: Holds 97% of Nayong county and 67% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 纳雍县…其中有穿青人20多万，占穿青人人口的1/3

regions.notes: Shuicheng (19% of the region) is already named on the map, so it is not offered. Only one good name found.

regions.summary: Zhijin county and part of Puding; already labelled.
